skin.setting: a Danube river steamer between two ports, 1908
skin.title: Death on the Blue Danube
skin.place: Aboard the river steamer SS Erzherzog Karl, bound for Budapest
skin.styleGuide: Austerity and Edwardian grandeur along misty river waters; polished mahogany, brass fittings, and gaslit interiors contrasted with cold river fog.

rooms.name: the Card Saloon
rooms.description: A velvet-draped salon fitted with baize card tables, polished spittoons, and heavy Austrian draperies.

rooms.name: the Grand Gallery
rooms.description: A long, paneled central vestibule illuminated by frosted glass lamps where the passenger cabins converge.

rooms.name: the Dining Saloon
rooms.description: A spacious hall arranged with damask-covered tables and gilded mirrors reflecting the river's dark swell.

rooms.name: the Reading Lounge
rooms.description: A quiet retreat lined with multilingual periodicals, leather armchairs, and brass reading lamps.

rooms.name: the Luggage Pantry
rooms.description: A narrow service room stacked with steamer trunks, heavy linens, and spare dining silver.

rooms.name: the Aft Promenade
rooms.description: An open deck space at the stern where chill river wind whips around iron railings and benches.

people.name: Baroness Von Brandt
people.bio: A haughty Viennese noblewoman traveling with lavish luggage and guarded secrets. She regards the other passengers with quiet condescension.
people.voice: Chilly, formal, and precise, laced with aristocratic impatience.
people.motive: The Count held promissory notes from her late husband that threatened her remaining estate.
people.portrait: A regal woman in an elaborate feathered hat and fur-trimmed velvet traveling gown.

people.name: Dr. Stefan Kovacs
people.bio: A Hungarian surgeon hired for the Danube crossing to attend first-class patrons. His calm exterior conceals a fraying personal ledger.
people.voice: Measured and clinical, delivering observations with detached professionalism.
people.motive: The Count discovered his medical malpractice in Pest and threatened to revoke his license.
people.portrait: A middle-aged man with a trimmed dark beard, wire spectacles, and a tweed waistcoat.

people.name: Captain Mihai Radu
people.bio: A seasoned river captain who has navigated the Danube's treacherous currents for decades. He is fiercely protective of his steamer's reputation.
people.voice: Gruff and authoritative, accustomed to barking orders across noisy river waters.
people.motive: The Count intended to buy a controlling stake in the shipping line and replace the veteran captain.
people.portrait: A broad-shouldered mariner in a double-breasted navy uniform with tarnished gold braid.

people.name: Clara Weiss
people.bio: A sharp-witted young woman employed in diplomatic circles in Vienna. She observes passenger movements with practiced discretion.
people.voice: Quiet, deferential, yet sharp and articulate under questioning.
people.motive: The Count had intercepted private correspondence that could ruin her career in the civil service.
people.portrait: A young woman with pinned auburn hair, high-collared blouse, and a leather notebook.

people.name: Josef Varga
people.bio: A timber magnate from the Banat traveling downriver to close an overdue grain trade. He carries a stout walking stick and a gruff demeanor.
people.voice: Blunt and deep, with a heavy rural accent and no patience for ceremony.
people.motive: The Count had double-crossed him on a lucrative timber concession along the lower Danube.
people.portrait: A stocky gentleman with thick moustaches, wearing a heavy wool overcoat and holding a carved walking cane.

people.name: Count Anton Bathory
people.bio: An influential Hungarian nobleman whose sharp dealings earned him enemies across the empire. His corpse was found collapsed in the central corridor.
people.portrait: An imposing nobleman with slicked silver hair, fine tailoring, and an expression of cold superiority.

silence: Baroness Von Brandt tilts her chin up. 'I have already recounted everything pertinent.'
Dr. Kovacs adjusts his spectacles. 'I have shared all the medical facts within my purview.'
Captain Radu scowls into his beard. 'I run a steamer, Inspector. I've told you what I saw.'
Clara Weiss shakes her head politely. 'I have nothing further noted down, sir.'
Josef Varga grunts. 'I told you my movements; I won't repeat myself.'
Count Anton Bathory is dead and can offer no words.
skin.briefing: As the SS Erzherzog Karl cuts through the dense autumn fog between Vienna and Budapest, a sudden cry echoes through the corridors. Count Anton Bathory has been found murdered in the Grand Gallery. With the river locks ahead and the steamer isolated in the dark waters of the Danube, no one could have boarded or fled. The passengers and crew remain confined to quarters while the truth of this night's movements is uncovered.
skin.scene: A misty paddle steamer slicing through dark Danube waters at night, its gaslit portholes glowing warmly through the cold river fog.
skin.summingUp:
The fog presses thick against the river glass tonight, but within these gaslit walls of polished mahogany and brass, the truth stands entirely distinct. Count Anton Bathory met his end here in the Grand Gallery because he held intercepted private correspondence—letters that posed absolute ruin to a promising career in the civil service. Yet it is the precise progression of the clock and location that leaves no room for doubt.

First, we look to Card 3, which narrows down when the murder happened and confirms plainly that the crime was not committed at Seven in the Evening, nor at Midnight.

Next, we know that both the killer and Count Anton Bathory were present together in the Grand Gallery at the moment of the deed. That single reality clears Baroness Von Brandt, Dr. Stefan Kovacs, Captain Mihai Radu, and Josef Varga, while also establishing that the murder was not at Eight in the Evening.

By that very same measure—the necessity of both the killer and Count Anton Bathory sharing the Grand Gallery when the blow fell—the murder was not at Eleven in the Evening. And following that exact truth to its conclusion, the murder was not at Ten in the Evening.

Only one hour and one person remain untouched by elimination. It was at Nine in the Evening, and the hand that struck him down was yours, Clara Weiss.
